All four items landed: I-0834, I-0835, I-0836 (memory), I-0837.

## Verdict: real progress, but the headline is over-billed

The Lean is sound. All four commits are honest at the statement level: no sorries, no axioms beyond `propext / Classical.choice / Quot.sound` (I re-ran `#print axioms` via lean-lsp on `ker_trivGluedEval` and `thetaTrivDataZero`), the module elaborates clean, and the root import is present. Claims 1, 2 and 4 survive intact; claim 3 survives as stated but not as billed; claim 5 has one real omission. The direction is right — this is a genuine de-confinement, not churn. But the inhabited case buys less than the commit messages and ADDENDUM 12 say, and two collapses at a = 0 were not measured.

### On your five questions

**1. `ThetaTrivData` chart-confining? No. CONFIRMED sound.** Read literally, `germ_read` (lines 120-126) quantifies `∀ (j) (b : Bool) (z) (hzj : z ∈ D.pieces j) (hzb : z ∈ relPinnedChart C R π b)` — the chart membership is a *hypothesis on the point*, not on the piece, and both `b` values are available at every point because `relCover_sup` gives `V₀ ⊔ V₁ = ⊤`. A straddling piece simply satisfies the field with different `b` at different `z`. That is structurally different from `piece_le : ∀ j, D.pieces j ≤ pinnedChartOfSide (side j)`, which universally quantifies the point inside a *fixed* chart per piece. Your ADDENDUM 12 §12.2 distinction (bundle model vs. divisor confinement) is the correct diagnosis. The `u` in `germ_read` is also allowed to depend on `x` (verified in the elaborated binder order), which is weaker still — that is fine here, but note it means `read j` is *not* forced to be a trivialization in any sheaf-theoretic sense; the docstring at line 100 calls it "a trivialization of `𝒪(Θᵃ)` over `pieces j`" and the field does not say that.

**2. `thetaTrivDataZero` unconditional? CONFIRMED yes.** Elaborated signature: `{k} [Field k] {C} {R} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R] {π} [IsFinite π] (D : AffCoverData C R) : ThetaTrivData D 0`. `existsUnique_glueThetaZero` has the same binder set and no cover hypothesis; `le_iSup_top_inf_relPinnedChart` is a statement about the curve. Nothing enters via instances beyond `IsFinite π`. It works on a straddling cover.

**3. The separation. Verified but the exponents are the defect.** Both halves hold and all four straddling hypotheses are load-bearing (`lean_minimal_hypotheses`). The asymmetry you flagged is real and it matters more than you priced it, because of what happens at a = 0:

```
trivGluedSubmodule A (D.thetaTrivDataZero) = A.gluedSubmodule
```
holds — I proved it, via `unitGluedSubmodule_one`, since `thetaTrivDataZero.unit = 1`. So at the only exponent the new index is inhabited, `TrivGlued / trivGluedEval / ker_trivGluedEval` all live on the **untwisted** equalizer `A.gluedSubmodule` that `DivisorFamilyAffAdaptation.lean:233` already defines. The re-indexing is correct and the old index maps in (`trivGluedSubmodule A (τ.thetaTrivData a) = thetaGluedSubmodule A τ a` by `rfl`, verified) — but the *inhabited* case computes an object the widened carrier already had. "Strictly wider" is true at exactly one exponent, and the twist is trivial there. Filed as I-0835.

**4. Same submodule? CONFIRMED, not glib.** `rw [ker_trivWindowCarve, ker_windowCarve]` closes `ker (trivWindowCarve A T hH1) = ker (windowCarve A τ a hH1)` under a *third*, independently-declared local `C.left.Over` instance in my scratch file. Both land on `divisorWindow d hH1` with no transport. This is the strongest of your five claims.

**5. ADDENDUM 12 — one real omission, plus a name error.** "Every widened cover carries one" is qualified by "at `a = 0`" everywhere it appears (§12.3 bullet, the file's line 53, both commit messages) — that check passes. §12.4's two limits are stated at full strength. What is missing is the limit you did not know to state:

`trivWindowCarve` and friends carry `hH1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1`. **At a = 0 that hypothesis forces genus 0.** Chain, all from declarations already in the tree and verified by me: `fieldToRelH1` → `thetaFieldH1PairEquiv` → `subsingleton_hModule_thetaTwistSheaf_one_iff` gives `Subsingleton H¹(divisorSheaf k (0 • fiberWeilDivisor π))`; then `zero_smul` and `Scheme.divisorSheafZeroIso` give `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪_C)`, which is `genus C = 0` by the definition at `Challenge.lean:89`. So on a positive-genus curve the produced datum and a satisfiable `hH1` never co-exist, and the window half of the re-indexed layer is unreachable through your own producer. `ker_trivGluedEval` carries no `hH1` and is unaffected. Filed as I-0834.

Relatedly, §12.4's "`a = 0` is nonetheless not a vacuous corner: it is the exponent `DivisorAdaptation.divisorDatum` reads the class at" is true but is about the *`FinCoverData`* carrier (`DivisorDatumInverse.lean:215`), not about this layer's consumers. The ε exponents are `windowM_choice` and `windowM_choice + windowS_choice` (`DivisorFamilyWindow.lean:260`), and I verified `windowM_choice π hπ g = 0` also forces `Subsingleton H¹(𝒪_C)`. So a = 0 is never an ε exponent on a curve of interest.

Also: the header bullet at line 53 cites `thetaTrivData_zero`, which does not exist (`AffCoverData.thetaTrivDataZero`) — I-0837.

### What this means for the next round

Not churning, not stuck — but the next iteration should not be more re-indexing. The single obligation that moves the lane is **inhabitation at a > 0**, which needs `𝒪(Θᵃ)` trivial over each arbitrary affine piece. Your file names it correctly as a bundle condition. Note the layer also still needs a widened `IsThetaPaired` witness at a > 0 (`DivisorFamilyAffTheta.lean:570`, unproved, and its own satisfiability probe `isThetaPaired_zero` sits at the same trivial corner) and surjectivity, so a > 0 inhabitation is necessary but not sufficient. The durable lesson — check inhabitation *and* what the inhabited instance costs the rest of the statement, since a bound stated for general `a` can degenerate at the corner where your producer lives — is I-0836.
